WTF Was Trump’s New Press Secretary Doing in China?
articles.description: It’s not clear if new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia ever actually worked as an attorney—but it is becoming increasingly clear that she was connected to the Chinese government in the past. Speaking alongside Donald Trump Tuesday, Zacharia informed reporters inquiring about her self-purported legal qualifications that she passed the bar exam when she “moved to China.” Popular Info’s Judd Legum found that, after analyzing state bar association databases from all 50 states and Washington, Zacharia never actually passed the qualifying legal exam anywhere in the country. But she couldn’t have passed the Chinese equivalent of the bar exam, either, as it’s actually forbidden for foreigners to do so. Zacharia’s LinkedIn work history places her at Zhong Lun, an elite Chinese multinational law firm, between 2011 and 2013. She worked at the Beijing-based firm as an associate on the international practice team, months after she obtained her J.D. from Pepperdine Caruso Law. Zacharia’s LinkedIn also notes that she spoke Chinese at an “elementary proficiency.” Like many major Chinese businesses, Zhong Lung operates in an environment in which it can be influenced by the regional government. Since it was founded in 1993, the firm has provided legal services to numerous Chinese government agencies and state-owned enterprises. Some of those entities include China’s Ministry of Justice, People’s Bank of China, the Ministry of Commerce, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Natural Resources, Ministry of Ecology and Environment, and other regulatory bodies, according to the firm’s webpage. Within that same time period, Zacharia also worked as the manager of fundraising and communications at Compassion for Migrant Children, a Beijing-based nonprofit that provided education and material support to rural migrant workers. The group also noted in an archived profile that it “engage[d] the Chinese government and local educational officials for greater and longer lasting impact.”

articles.title: White House enraged after Kaitlan Collins shares embarrassing clip of Trump's empty seats
articles.description: For the second time in three days, the White House is blaming the press for the empty seats at a Trump rally. The White House’s Rapid Response 47 account hit back at CNN’s Kaitlan Collins after she aired footage of bare upper sections at President Donald Trump’s Monday night rally in Youngstown, Ohio. “The only one humiliated here is @kaitlancollins. These ‘vacant seats’ had an obstructed view due to the gigantic press risers directly in front of them. Just more Fake News bulls---,” the account posted on X. The account made nearly the same claim days earlier. After New York Times reporter Shawn McCreesh posted video of whole empty sections at Trump’s rally in Clarksville, Tennessee on Saturday, Rapid Response said those seats were “purposely left empty” because anyone sitting in them would have had their view blocked by “gigantic press risers,” the Irish Star reported. The Youngstown explanation doesn’t account for local reporting. Station WFMJ found that tarps covered roughly a quarter of the Covelli Centre’s seating, and that the crowd never filled more than about two-thirds of the seats left open. The Tribune Chronicle estimated 2,500 to 3,000 people attended, compared with roughly 7,000 at Trump’s 2017 rally in the same arena. The paper also reported that about half the permanent seats were closed off before the event began. Collins had allowed on “The Source” that it was hard to know how much to read into the turnout. She noted that Trump is the one who has been claiming his events need big overflow rooms. The press riser defense is the latest in a string of explanations. Last week, Trump insisted that supporters seated up high routinely “migrate down to the Main Floor” and declared that he never has empty seats. Collins has been a frequent target. Trump mocked her looks at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner in July and told her to “smile.” The fight over the crowd comes as Republicans scramble to hold Ohio. A CNN poll released last week showed Democrat Sherrod Brown leading Republican Sen. Jon Husted 49 percent to 43 percent among likely voters.

articles.title: Goldman sees Europe reserve release cutting diesel by $11 but shrugs off Russian supply
articles.description: Diesel remains the sharpest pressure point in the energy shock from the Iran war, and Goldman’s view suggests relief depends on government stockpiles rather than extra Russian barrels. A European reserve release of the scale Goldman models would offer meaningful but temporary relief, narrowing refining margins and easing pressure on transport and industrial costs feeding into inflation. The bank’s broader view that product markets stay tight into 2027 means any relief rally in diesel could prove short-lived, keeping crack spreads elevated and refiners’ margins strong. For crude, a sustained diesel squeeze keeps demand for refinery runs high, supporting oil prices even if headline supply fears ease. --- Earlier: More on Russia’s diesel U-turn: 500,000 tons cleared for export after Trump-Putin deal IEA urges faster diesel releases as 400m-barrel March pledge lags, board meets Oct 15 ---- Goldman’s message on diesel is that Europe’s emergency stockpiles can take some heat out of prices, but Moscow’s offer won’t, and the underlying shortage is not going away soon. Summary: Goldman Sachs said it does not expect Russia’s announced diesel releases to have a significant impact on global diesel prices The bank estimates a potential 50 million barrel release of diesel from Europe’s strategic reserves could lower US Gulf Coast and European wholesale diesel prices by $11 a barrel Russia recently said it could supply more diesel to global markets, with exports potentially reaching 3 to 3.5 million tonnes by year-end, amid talks with the US G7 members agreed on 2 October to release 100 million barrels of diesel and other reserves over four months, with a front-loaded diesel release In an earlier note, Goldman said diesel could stay expensive through 2027, with refining margins potentially averaging above $40 a barrel Goldman Sachs said it does not expect Russia’s planned diesel releases to have a significant impact on global diesel prices, but estimated that drawing down Europe’s strategic diesel stocks could offer more meaningful relief. The bank estimated that a potential release of 50 million barrels of diesel from Europe’s strategic reserves could lower wholesale diesel prices on the US Gulf Coast and in Europe by about $11 a barrel. Russia has recently signalled it could supply more diesel to global markets. Russian officials said last week that talks with the US government were under way on supply and that Russian diesel exports could reach 3 million to 3.5 million tonnes by year-end. Goldman’s assessment suggests those volumes are too small to shift the balance in a market that remains severely stretched. Diesel has been at the centre of the energy shock triggered by the war involving Iran. Disruption to Middle East supply, attacks on refining infrastructure and export restrictions in several countries have pushed prices to records. US diesel reached about $6.50 a gallon late last month, while European prices hit record highs. Governments have already moved to respond. Group of Seven members agreed on 2 October to release 100 million barrels of diesel and other reserves through the International Energy Agency over four months, with a substantial diesel release front-loaded into the first 20 days. Goldman’s estimate indicates how much difference a European diesel release on the scale it models could make to prices. The bank’s latest view builds on a series of notes on the refined products market. In late September, Goldman said a US ban on diesel exports, which it called plausible but not its base case, would lower US prices while raising them in Europe. In a note published earlier this month, the bank warned that diesel could remain expensive through 2027, as global refining capacity struggles to meet recovering demand while depleted inventories are rebuilt. It said margins on diesel and jet fuel could average above $40 a barrel next year, more than double their usual level, and that the G7 release would ease pressure only temporarily without fixing the structural shortfall. Together, the notes point to a market where emergency stocks can buy time, but lasting relief depends on refinery capacity and a recovery in Middle East supply. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.
